text: Chest pain in adults may indicate acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Red flags include radiating pain, diaphoresis, hypotension, and troponin elevation. Shortness of breath with wheezing suggests obstructive airway disease. Consider asthma exacerbation, COPD, or pulmonary embolism if tachycardic or hypoxic. NSAIDs can increase bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulants. Avoid pairing unless clinically necessary and monitor INR/bleeding signs.
